methods: Design: cross-sectional analysis of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic. Population: Age >=18 years; excluding pregnant at examination (analytic n = 6,610). Outcome: HbA1c. Exposure: Waist circumference. Comparator: per-unit contrast along the exposure (lower vs higher values); quartiles as sensitivity. Covariates: Age, Sex, Race and ethnicity, Income-to-poverty ratio, Educational attainment, Smoking status, Body mass index. Descriptive: survey-weighted Table 1 by abdominal obesity - waist >102 cm (men) / >88 cm (women); weighted prevalence with 95% CIs. Model: mean differences (survey-weighted linear regression); sequential models: Unadjusted, Adjusted for age, sex, and race and ethnicity, Fully adjusted (primary). Effect modification: interaction tests and stratified estimates by sex, age group. Survey design: Taylor linearisation with strata and PSUs; weight WTMECPRP; design df = 25. Sensitivity analyses (8): Binary outcome: Elevated HbA1c (>=6.5%) (PR); Exclude participants on glucose-lowering therapy; Exclude anemia (HbA1c unreliable); Multiple imputation of missing covariates (m = 10); Exposure in weighted quartiles (Q4 vs Q1, P for trend); Alternative exposure: Abdominal obesity - waist >102 cm (men) / >88 cm (women); Alternative exposure: Central adiposity - waist-to-height ratio >=0.5; Unweighted analysis (design ignored). Missing data: complete-case primary analysis; multiple imputation as sensitivity. Reporting: STROBE; plan pre-registered by hash before data access.

limitations.text: Cross-sectional: exposure and outcome are measured at the same visit, so the direction of association cannot be established.
Residual and unmeasured confounding cannot be excluded in an observational analysis.
Laboratory values come from a single blood or urine sample; transient abnormalities may be misclassified as persistent.
Complete-case loss: 17.3% of the analytic sample (1378) lack >=1 covariate. Multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis recommended.
Raw values within plausible ranges: Out-of-range values: BMXBMI (0 low, 1 high); LBXGH (1 low, 0 high)
Collinearity (generalized VIF): Maximum VIF 8.46 (waist_per10). Consider removing/combining collinear covariates or interpreting with care.

Sensitivity analyses agree with primary result: 7 of 8 sensitivity analyses agree in direction (associations) or magnitude (prevalence). Divergent: Alternative exposure: Central adiposity - waist-to-height ratio >=0.5

certainty.meaning: The true association is probably close to the estimate, but may be substantially different.

domains.reason: Cross-sectional design already reflected in the Low starting level; adjusted, pre-specified analysis with design audit passed.
Direction and inference stable across 6 sensitivity analyses.
US civilian non-institutionalised population; outcome measured directly.
Cannot be judged from a single study; pre-registration by plan hash reduces selective reporting.

rating_up.reason: Gradient across exposure quartiles (P for trend <.001).

certainty.caveat: GRADE rates bodies of evidence; this single-study rating summarises how much this analysis can contribute and should be re-rated in any systematic review.

assumptions: Design effect 1.8 (typical for NHANES; the post-run check uses the actual design-based SE).
